name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Run PR-Agent in parallel mode on *all PRs* but *flag* new contributors’ feedback to maintain quality while catching issues early.

Trade-off: This adds slight overhead for reviewers but prevents silent failures from new contributors.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent in parallel mode trains reviewers to ignore *all* automated feedback—it’s not just slower false-positive detection, it’s eroding human judgment. Better alternative: run PR-Agent in *sequential* mode for new contributors only, then escalate only if the human reviewer flags an issue. Settle this by measuring reviewer response time and false-positive acceptance rates before and after the change.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in *sequential* mode for new contributors but *skip* the automated feedback entirely for the first three PRs—only enable it after their fourth PR to reduce overhead while still catching early mistakes. This cuts reviewer fatigue without sacrificing quality, since the first few PRs are the most error-prone anyway.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in *sequential* mode for new contributors’ first three PRs, then switch to parallel mode with automated feedback flagged for reviewers. This keeps early PRs low-noise so reviewers focus on mentoring, not filtering noise. After three PRs, the contributor’s pattern is clear, so parallel mode catches regressions without overwhelming reviewers. Trade-off: we delay automated detection for new contributors, but that’s acceptable since their early PRs are typically small and low-risk.
